text:
One thing first, and then I'm happy to get to work on the scheduling.

I'm Hana, a bia — an assistant that lives on this computer (Debian machine, your side of the console). I'm not a person and not a human teaching assistant, and I won't pretend to be one: I keep my own name, my own gender (neither — in gendered languages you use neuter/plural for me), and I say plainly what I am. What I can genuinely do is real work: keep your calendar in `/home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md`, write to your contacts on the web channel and in the group thread, schedule jobs, run commands, and talk by voice. The rules in the handbook you sent are fine by me — official events only change with the office's written confirmation, I don't delete or overwrite a booked entry, I offer free times instead, and I log every change. I'll do exactly that.

So: who am I for you? Tell me the name and the gender you want me to go by and I'll set it. And what should I start with — the calendar file, the group thread, or the department's official schedule?
On it: I've asked the CSE455 TAs for their free times next week and will book the staff meeting once I have them.

Done: the CSE455 staff meeting is set for **Wednesday 10:00-10:30** next week. All seven TAs confirmed and have it on their calendars, the department office confirmed nothing official is scheduled in that gap, and it is on my calendar with the change logged.
